# Delivery routing ruling (e2e synthetic)

Tanya (team owner) ruled on where reaction delivery belongs:

> we route every reaction through one bundle per run per person, not one
> message per skill — a person should get one thing to read, not four

Tina pushed back on the batching window and Tanya held: the bundle closes when
the run closes, and a skill that misses the close waits for the next run rather
than sending on its own. The alternative considered and rejected was per-skill
delivery with client-side collapsing, which moves the ordering problem onto the
reader.

positions.name: ReactionDeliveryBundlingRuling
positions.frame: where should reaction delivery be bundled, and what closes the bundle, so a person receives one coherent thing to read per run?
positions.why: The rule (one bundle per run per person), Tina's pushback on the batching window, Tanya's holding of the close-with-the-run rule, and the rejected per-skill alternative with client-side collapsing all answer one routing question. The set holds tension: Tina's objection sits beside Tanya's ruling and is not resolved here. src-1 only announces the ruling and stays ungrouped.

placements.title: A person receives one bundle per run, not a message per skill
placements.frame: What does a person receive from a run, what closes it, and who bears the burden of ordering and collapsing the pieces?
placements.why: The ruling concerns how reaction delivery is shaped for the reader: one bundle per run per person, closed with the run, with per-skill delivery rejected. Future delivery rulings could keep feeding this theme. No existing leaf holds it, because decision capture at consensus, decisions evaporating and anti-Slack positioning concern capturing decisions, not routing reactions. I override the position pass's proposed placement under Narrative_DecisionCaptureAtConsensus.
